hints: Focus on how an ester splits during hydrolysis, with one part becoming the acid and the other part becoming the alcohol.
Notice that ethanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, so the left-hand acyl part of the ester must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$.
Now match the right-hand alkoxy part to butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and see which formula joins those two pieces together.
walkthrough:
**Recall ester hydrolysis**

Think of an ester as an acid joined to an alcohol with water removed. Adding water back splits it apart again.

General rule:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

**Find the acid part**

We need ethanoic acid, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. That means the $\text{RCO}_2$ part must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$.

So we can narrow down to esters starting with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$.

**Find the alcohol part**

We need butan-2-ol, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. In the ester this appears without the OH hydrogen as $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

So the $\text{R'}$ group must be $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Put the two parts together**

Join the acid fragment and the alcohol fragment to rebuild the ester:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2 + \text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
That structure hydrolyses to exactly the two required products.

options.A: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$. The acid part is correct for ethanoic acid, but the alcohol part gives propan-2-ol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHOH}$, not butan-2-ol. It has only three carbons in the alcohol.
options.B: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Hydrolysis gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ (ethanoic acid) plus $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (butan-2-ol). Both fragments match perfectly.
options.C: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Hydrolysis gives 2-methylpropanoic acid plus ethanol. Both the acid and the alcohol are wrong here, a common trap if you do not split the ester at the $\text{CO}_2$ group.
options.D: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The alcohol part is correct for butan-2-ol, but the acid part gives propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, not ethanoic acid.
